question: A small charged conducting sphere carrying charge $q$ is placed inside a larger hollow conducting shell carrying charge $Q$. If the two are connected by a wire, why does the charge $q$ flow entirely to the outer shell regardless of the magnitude or sign of $Q$?

options.A: Because the outer shell has a larger capacitance.
options.B: Because the potential of the inner sphere is always higher than that of the outer shell due to the term $q(1/r - 1/R)$.
options.C: Because the outer shell is grounded.
options.D: Because like charges attract in this specific configuration.
